Write an email to a colleague about not being discouraged by setbacks. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: A word about the setbacks

Dear Daniel,

I have been thinking about you since our conversation on Tuesday, and I want to put down in writing what I tried to say then, because I do not think I said it as well as I should have.

You told me that the loss of the Henderson contract had taken the heart out of the team, and that you were beginning to wonder whether the new approach was the right one after all. I want you to make up your mind, before all things else, that you are not going to let one disappointment, or even two or three, turn you aside from the work that is before you. There is nothing, then, to be discouraged about. We are going forward, and we shall keep going forward.

I have found, in my own experience, that the difficulties which seem the largest at the moment are the ones we are least likely to remember a year from now. What we do remember is whether we stood firm when the difficulty came. Nobody who is worthy of respect has ever reached that position without meeting a great many obstacles on the way, and without meeting them in a patient and cheerful spirit. The people whom we most admire in our own field are, almost without exception, the ones who were refused again and again and who simply went back to work the next morning.

I would ask you to do two things. First, sit down with the team this week and go over the Henderson matter very carefully, from every point of view, and find out honestly what was lacking. Do not be hard on anyone, yourself least of all, but do not be careless about it either. A failure that is looked at squarely is worth ten times more than a success that is never examined. Second, let the team see that you are not discouraged. They will take their tone from you. If you are steady, they will be steady; if you are downcast, they will be downcast, and the loss will then be twice as great as it was at the start.

Just in proportion as we show that we can bear a reverse without losing our courage, the good things will come to us. I am sure of it, and I hope you will let me know how the meeting goes.

Yours sincerely,

Thomas
